correctness.rationale: Every nonzero periodic labeled word has exactly one state lift, while the zero word has r lifts if \(r\) divides its period and none otherwise, yielding \(p_n\) and ordinary zeta. A complete half-cycle bijection gives interior-gap \(L(z)=z/(1-z^r)\), vertex-end \(1+B\), edge-end \(A\), and free interior continuation \(C(z)=(1-L(z))^{-1}\). These produce the three stated exact rational series for every integer \(r\ge2\); parity follows from \(2h\equiv1\pmod r\) with explicit witnesses. Direct extraction/run of independent exact integer verifier checks 322 comparisons for \(2\le r\le8\); these tests support but do not replace the unrestricted bijective proof.

value.rationale: Reversal-fixed period counts and Lind zeta are natural dynamical conjugacy invariants. The theorem provides all three reflection-axis statistics in explicit rational form for unbounded modular alphabet parameter r, plus a sharp parity phenomenon that changes which vertex-axis symmetric periodic states can exist. The odd-modulus witnesses make it a genuine structural boundary, not just a formatting simplification of a known single even-shift expression. A general sofic matrix algorithm does not itself articulate this concrete obstruction or furnish its uniform simplification; however the result does not claim new generic existence or rationality.
